summary: Carefully preregistered, artifact-backed paired study that evaluated a generate–verify–repair guardrail under explicit shared_initial_candidate semantics. Execution and archived artifacts appear internally consistent and reproducible; the primary confirmatory result is a near-null paired improvement (1/250 discordant pair). Main deficiencies are presentation/provenance clarity (reference formatting, a confusing provider-call accounting field, and an abstract/labeling mismatch about which preregistered partitions were actually executed). These can be corrected from the supplied artifacts without new experiments.
critical_issues: References are not presented as a conventional IEEE numbered bibliography with full bibliographic metadata; manuscript currently records bare DOIs/arXiv/identifier-style entries. This violates the conference/reference requirements and prevents independent verification of in-text citation semantics.

A provider-call/accounting field in the archived manifest (provider_call_audit.condition_counts shows {'shared':250,'guarded':1}) is inconsistent with the reported paired episode accounting (completed_episode_count=500, complete_pair_count=250) and with the reported guarded_success_count=250. This discrepancy can confuse readers and reviewers into thinking conditions had independent first-pass generations; it must be reconciled or clearly explained in Methods using existing artifacts.

Abstract and some metadata/title wording risk implying a broader sim-to-real or vendor-heterogeneity confirmatory evaluation, while the preregistered confirmatory execution and the archived run applied only to the synthetic/emulation partition. The manuscript must clearly and unambiguously state in the Abstract (and any headings that reference the preregistration title) that the confirmatory run covered the emulation/synthetic partition only and that other partitions remained exploratory/unexecuted.
required_revisions: Replace the References section with a conventional IEEE numbered bibliography (authors, title, venue, year, DOI/arXiv) derived from the archived/verifiable records; update all in-text citations to use those IEEE numeric markers and ensure each cited work actually supports the nearby claim (use the verified evidence records preserved in the archive to construct entries).

Add a short, explicit Methods clarification (can be a paragraph) that reconciles the provider_call_audit fields with the shared_initial_candidate execution semantics using the archived provider-call and stage-count artifacts. Specifically: explain that model_calls_used=251 consists of 250 shared_initial_generation calls plus 1 repair call; explain the meaning of provider_call_audit.condition_counts and confirm that the same sampled initial candidate was used for both baseline and guarded episodes per pair (no independent first-pass generation per condition). Point reviewers to the archived manifest paths/hashes for verification (do not paste logs).

Edit the Abstract to state unambiguously that the confirmatory experiment was executed on the synthetic/emulation partition only (as preregistered) and that community and production-like partitions in the preregistration were exploratory and not executed in this confirmatory run. Ensure the Introduction/Title do not imply a completed sim-to-real or production-like confirmatory contrast if those partitions were not executed.
optional_revisions: In Results or Discussion, briefly note that the exact McNemar two-sided p-value of 1.0 arises from the very small count of discordant pairs (n10+n01=1) and so is uninformative for ruling out small effects; emphasize the paired CI and the preregistered power mismatch as the primary inferential constraints.

Condense the Disclosure Statement slightly to remove any text that duplicates archive inventory details (the preregistration SHA and master-prompt SHA are sufficient identifiers; refer to the archived evidence bundle for full manifests).

Correct or annotate any minor manifest-field naming inconsistencies (e.g., condition_counts vs stage_counts) so automated readers and auditors do not misinterpret fields; a one-sentence note in Methods is sufficient.

If space permits, add a one-line mapping table (in the manuscript or an evidence appendix) from numbered citations to the corresponding archived verification-record identifiers to strengthen reference-integrity transparency without reproducing logs.
